heading: A Doctor. A Problem Solver. A Voice for Every Family
text: Fix the traffic. Stop the flooding. Healthcare for all. Make life affordable

heading: Meet Neil
text: Neil Manimala grew up in Valrico, the son of a nurse and a respiratory therapist who worked opposite hospital shifts to raise their two boys. He graduated from Hillsborough County public schools, earned his degrees at USF, and became a board-certified urologist. Today he cares for patients across Brandon, Plant City, and Sun City Center, and he serves as the 123rd President of the Hillsborough County Medical Association. Neil became a doctor to keep people healthy. Then he watched broken politics undo that work. His patients miss appointments because of the impossible choice of paying for groceries or gas versus their medication or surgery.

heading: Meet Neil
text: Families lose homes to floods that better planning would have prevented. Neighbors put off their own healthcare because they can barely afford childcare. Neil approaches the county the way he approaches medicine. He finds the cause, treats it, and follows up until it is fixed.

heading: Meet Dr. Neil Manimala
text: Neil Manimala is the son of immigrants who both worked in healthcare. His mother was a nurse and his father a respiratory therapist, and they worked opposite hospital shifts to raise their family in Valrico.

heading: Meet Dr. Neil Manimala
text: Neil graduated from Hillsborough County public schools and earned his undergraduate and medical degrees at the University of South Florida. Today Neil is a board-certified urologist caring for patients across Brandon, Riverview, Plant City, and Sun City Center. He serves as the 123rd President of the Hillsborough County Medical Association, and he has served the county on the Health Care Advisory Board and the Health Council of West Central Florida.

heading: Meet Dr. Neil Manimala
text: In the clinic, Neil never asks his patients who they voted for. He asks where it hurts. And year after year, he hears the same answers. Patients skip medication to afford groceries. Families lose homes to floods that better planning would have prevented. Parents put off their own care to cover childcare. Neil became a doctor to keep people healthy, and he watched broken politics undo that work. So he is doing what doctors do. He examines the problem, finds the cause, and treats it, and he follows up until it is fixed. That is not politics as usual. That is how a healer works.

heading: Meet Dr. Neil Manimala
text: Neil and his wife Rachel, a nurse, live here with their baby daughter Mariam and their rescue dog Benji. They are parishioners at Sacred Heart Catholic Church. As a new father, Neil is running to build a county where families can afford to stay, seniors can age with dignity, and the next generation can put down roots and thrive.
